+---
+description: "CSS clean-code and theming rules for the Solitaire app."
+applyTo: "**/*.css"
+---
+# CSS rules
+
+## Theming
+
+- Components use only semantic CSS custom properties, such as
+  `--color-surface`, `--color-text`, `--color-accent`, or `--space-md`.
+  Never use raw color values inside component rules.
+- Themes define those properties under `:root[data-theme="<name>"]`.
+  The default theme is also defined on plain `:root`.
+- Adding a theme must require only a new set of property values, not component
+  changes.
+
+## Structure
+
+- Sizes and spacing come from shared custom properties.
+- Prefix class names with their component, such as `.notification-card`.
+- Never style by ID.
+- Write mobile-first: base rules for small screens, `min-width` media queries
+  for larger ones.
+
+## Motion and focus
+
+- Animations follow the user's animation setting (Slide, Fade, or None).
+- Never remove a focus outline without a visible replacement; use
+  `:focus-visible` for keyboard focus styling.

+---
+description: "HTML semantics, accessibility, and keyboard-navigation rules for the Solitaire app."
+applyTo: "**/*.html"
+---
+# HTML rules
+
+The same rules apply to markup created from JavaScript.
+
+## Semantics
+
+- Use meaningful elements: `<button>` for actions, `<a>` for navigation,
+  `<dialog>` for modals, and headings in order.
+- Every control has an accessible name that screen readers can announce.
+
+## Keyboard navigation
+
+- Every interactive control can be reached with Tab and operated with the
+  keyboard.
+- Tab order follows the visual order. Never use a positive `tabindex`.
+- Focus is always visible.
+- Modals move focus inside when opened, keep it there while open, and return it
+  to the opening control when closed. Escape and clicking outside the modal
+  close it.
+- Menus close when the user clicks outside the open menu.
+
+## Scripts
+
+- Load application scripts as `<script type="module">`.
+- Asset URLs carry the release `?v=` stamp; never add or edit stamps by hand.

+---
+description: "JavaScript clean-code rules for the Solitaire app and its browser tests."
+applyTo: "docs/**/*.js, tests/**/*.js"
+---
+# JavaScript rules
+
+Follow `ARCHITECTURE.md` for module structure, import rules, and the game contract.
+
+## Reuse before writing
+
+- Before writing a helper, check the shared-code catalog in `ARCHITECTURE.md`.
+  Use an existing export instead of re-implementing it.
+- When you add, rename, or remove a shared export, update the catalog in the
+  same change.
+- Keep game-specific code inside its game folder until a second game needs it.
+
+## Modules
+
+- Use native ES modules (`<script type="module">`, `import`/`export`). No
+  bundler, transpiler, Node runtime, or build step.
+- Use named exports. No default exports and no global variables.
+- Import with relative paths that include the `.js` extension.
+- Each module has one responsibility.
+- Shared modules start with a one-line `/** @module ... */` summary.
+
+## Game logic stays pure
+
+- Rule functions take a state and return a new state. Never mutate inputs.
+- Rule modules never touch the DOM, IndexedDB, timers, randomness, or the clock.
+  Pass such values in as arguments.
+
+## Syntax
+
+- `const` by default, `let` only when reassigned, never `var`.
+- Always use strict equality (`===`, `!==`).
+- Write small functions; return early instead of nesting.
+- Give fixed numbers a named constant instead of a bare literal.
+
+## Naming
+
+- camelCase for functions and variables.
+- PascalCase for classes.
+- UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for constants.
+- kebab-case for file names.
+
+## Comments and types
+
+- Comments explain *why*, not *what*.
+- Exported functions have JSDoc type annotations (`@param`, `@returns`,
+  `@typedef`) so the editor can check types without a build step.
+
+## Errors
+
+- Never swallow an error.
+- Handle failures where the app meets the browser or IndexedDB.
+- Show the user a short, friendly message through the notification system.
+- Log the full error with context to the console with `console.error`.
+
+## Dependencies
+
+- No third-party runtime libraries without owner approval.
+- Load nothing from external servers or CDNs at runtime; everything ships in `docs/`.
+
+## Tests
+
+- Test pure logic with the in-repo browser test runner in `tests/`.
+- Tests live outside `docs/` and are never deployed.

+# Generated by project-toolkit
+# Source: https://github.com/Ignyos/project-toolkit
+# Commit: 0c9e12c7b9fd60e297e690b5a3943edabe8dc868
+# Profile: vanilla-js-github-pages-spa
+# Generated: 2026-10-12T22:06:35Z
+name: Deploy Dev Site
+on:
+  push:
+    branches: [dev]
+  workflow_dispatch:
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+concurrency:
+  group: deploy-dev-pages
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+jobs:
+  deploy-dev:
+    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/dev'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+      - name: Validate production source and dev target
+        shell: pwsh
+        env:
+          DEV_PAGES_REPO: ${{ secrets.DEV_PAGES_REPO }}
+          DEV_PAGES_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEV_PAGES_TOKEN }}
+        run: |
+          & .\build.ps1
+          $config = Import-PowerShellDataFile .\deploy-config.psd1
+          if ($env:DEV_PAGES_REPO -cne $config.DevRepository) {
+            throw 'DEV_PAGES_REPO must match the separate repository in deploy-config.psd1.'
+          }
+          if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($env:DEV_PAGES_TOKEN)) {
+            throw 'DEV_PAGES_TOKEN is required.'
+          }
+          if ($config.DevRepository -ieq '${{ github.repository }}') {
+            throw 'Dev deployment cannot target the source/production repository.'
+          }
+          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path .\.pages-dev -Force | Out-Null
+          Copy-Item -Path .\docs\* -Destination .\.pages-dev -Recurse
+          Set-Content -LiteralPath .\.pages-dev\CNAME -Value $config.DevDomain -NoNewline
+      - name: Publish staging copy to external dev repository root
+        uses: peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v4
+        with:
+          personal_token: ${{ secrets.DEV_PAGES_TOKEN }}
+          external_repository: ${{ secrets.DEV_PAGES_REPO }}
+          publish_branch: main
+          publish_dir: ./.pages-dev
+          force_orphan: true

+# Generated by project-toolkit
+# Source: https://github.com/Ignyos/project-toolkit
+# Commit: 0c9e12c7b9fd60e297e690b5a3943edabe8dc868
+# Profile: vanilla-js-github-pages-spa
+# Generated: 2026-10-12T22:06:35Z
+name: Create Release
+on:
+  push:
+    tags: ['*']
+permissions:
+  contents: write
+jobs:
+  create-release:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          persist-credentials: false
+      - name: Verify production timestamp release
+        shell: pwsh
+        env:
+          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
+        run: |
+          if ($env:RELEASE_TAG -notmatch '^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-\d{2}-\d{2}$') {
+            throw 'Only bare UTC timestamp release tags are supported.'
+          }
+          git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main
+          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Release commit must be in main history.' }
+          & .\build.ps1
+          $html = Get-Content .\docs\index.html -Raw
+          $worker = Get-Content .\docs\service-worker.js -Raw
+          if (-not $html.Contains("?v=$env:RELEASE_TAG") -or
+              -not $worker.Contains("const CACHE_NAME = 'solitaire-v$env:RELEASE_TAG';")) {
+            throw 'Release tag must match asset/cache identity.'
+          }
+          if (-not (Test-Path ".\release\rel-$env:RELEASE_TAG.txt")) {
+            throw 'Release diff audit is required.'
+          }
+          $notes = Get-Content .\RELEASE_NOTES.md -Raw
+          if ($notes -notmatch "(?m)^# Release $([regex]::Escape($env:RELEASE_TAG))\s*$") {
+            throw 'Release notes timestamp must match the tag.'
+          }
+      - name: Create GitHub Release
+        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
+        with:
+          body_path: RELEASE_NOTES.md
+          fail_on_unmatched_files: true
+          files: release/rel-${{ github.ref_name }}.txt

+# Solitaire agent guidance
+
+Solitaire is a static vanilla JavaScript browser application/PWA served from `docs/`.
+The initial scaffold does not implement gameplay. Preserve the existing license.
+
+## Source of truth and workflow
+
+- Read `PM/project-management.md` and the indexed item files before discussing status,
+  priorities, or choosing work. The `current/` index owns active work; do not duplicate
+  item ids or status here.
+- Follow `PM/workflow.md` for lifecycle, developer confirmation, and deployment checkpoints.
+- Branching Policy: enabled, see `PM/branching.md`.
+- Read `README.md` for local tooling and external deployment prerequisites.
+- Never commit, switch branches, merge, or push on the developer's behalf without approval.
+
+## Architecture and safeguards
+
+- Use native HTML, CSS, and JavaScript without a compilation step. Keep deployed assets in `docs/`.
+- Follow `ARCHITECTURE.md` for code structure, the game contract, and the shared-code
+  catalog. Check the catalog before writing new helpers; update it with shared exports.
+- Follow the coding rules in `.github/instructions/` (JavaScript, CSS, HTML).
+- `REQUIREMENTS.md` owns application behavior.
+- `deploy-config.psd1` owns deployment targets. `main` is production; `dev` deploys only
+  to the external dev repository. The tracked `docs/CNAME` must remain production-only.
+- Use `build.ps1` to validate. Use `dev-publish.ps1` and `release.ps1` for publishing,
+  not ad hoc version or tag updates. A single UTC `yyyy-MM-dd-HH-mm` stamp identifies
+  assets, service worker caches, release diffs, and tags.
+- Non-main release runs are read-only rehearsals. Live releases require a clean tree,
+  diff-grounded release notes, and explicit confirmation before committing or tagging.
+- Keep preview banner behavior and offline cache invalidation consistent when changing assets.
+- Preserve toolkit origin breadcrumbs during maintenance.

+# Solitaire architecture
+
+This document owns code structure: shared versus game-specific code, import
+rules, the game contract, and the catalog of reusable shared code. Product
+behavior lives in `REQUIREMENTS.md`; coding style lives in
+`.github/instructions/`.
+
+## Platform
+
+- Static site on GitHub Pages; no server backend, Node runtime, bundler, or
+  build step.
+- Native ES modules loaded by the browser.
+- Release-stamped `?v=` URLs apply to module import paths as well as to
+  `<script>`/`<link>` tags, so a release never mixes cached old modules with new
+  ones. The release scripts and service worker must support this before the
+  first module ships.
+- Pure logic is tested by an in-repo, dependency-free browser test runner in
+  `tests/`, opened through the local dev server and never deployed.
+
+## Approved core contracts at a glance
+
+- **Platform:** static GitHub Pages app; native browser ES modules; no server,
+  Node runtime, bundler, or runtime CDN dependencies.
+- **Code boundaries:** shared code never imports games; games may use shared
+  code but never import another game. Game logic is pure. Consult the
+  shared-code catalog before adding reusable helpers.
+- **Storage:** one IndexedDB database, with one shared settings store and one
+  object store per game. Shared storage owns connection/transaction mechanics;
+  settings and game repositories own their domain operations and schemas.
+- **Durable actions:** board snapshot and undo history change atomically.
+  Automatic consequences are part of the action's undo step. Winning or
+  forfeiting records the outcome and deletes move history atomically.
+- **Write safety:** one writable window; Web Locks with a tested, fail-closed
+  fallback and transactional revision checks. Revision conflicts stop play and
+  offer to load the latest save, not retry stale actions.
+- **Save failures:** shared coordinator retries the same atomic operation up to
+  three times, one second apart, each in a fresh transaction. On final failure,
+  block moves and offer manual Retry or Revert to the last save.
+- **Settings:** definitions provide defaults and validation. Missing values
+  read as defaults without writes; invalid values are rejected. Game-home option
+  changes save immediately as that game's last-selected settings; each deal
+  stores its actual options.
+- **Notifications:** callers supply type, friendly message, and optional
+  required actions; the notification service owns timers, stack policy, and
+  settings-driven display. Errors affecting current use are surfaced; unrelated
+  background cache failures remain quiet.
+- **Modals and menus:** separate services. Modals use `<dialog>` and own focus,
+  Escape, outside-click, and return-value lifecycle. The persistent application
+  menu is top-left, distinct from a game's in-game menu.
+- **Navigation:** hash routes for Home, game home, and an attempt. A valid
+  explicit route wins on startup; otherwise restore the last stable saved view.
+  Stable navigation waits for pending writes; transient overlays are not saved.
+- **Offline and updates:** verify every required same-origin asset in the
+  release manifest; show readiness persistently in Install App (Help), and keep
+  unrelated cache repair quiet. Updates wait until old clients close and apply
+  on next launch without an update prompt. Migrations preserve data and report
+  failure without adding specialized recovery workflows.
+- **Themes:** semantic CSS custom properties with a default theme and optional
+  token-only overrides; no theme framework.
+- **Game scope:** Klondike is first. Its implementation validates the
+  provisional folder structure and informs the reusable game implementation
+  guide.
+
+## Validation boundary
+
+The approved product behavior and service responsibilities above are the
+current contract. Implementation mechanisms remain provisional until exercised
+by the first game (Klondike), including:
+
+- Exact storage record schemas, indexes, and module API signatures.
+- The folder/module layout and game contract details beyond approved
+  responsibilities.
+- Cross-browser writable-window fallback mechanics.
+- Cache verification, asset-manifest generation, and service-worker lifecycle
+  implementation details.
+
+Klondike implementation may refine these mechanisms based on demonstrated
+needs. It must not silently change approved user-visible behavior; behavioral
+changes return to owner discussion.
+
+## Core contract acceptance checklist
+
+Use this checklist when core services are implemented. Each result is
+observable at the UI or durable-state boundary; tests should not depend on
+internal helper names or the provisional folder layout.
+
+### Startup and navigation
+
+- [ ] Startup renders the application shell without waiting for service-worker
+  registration or cache repair.
+- [ ] IndexedDB upgrades complete before settings/context are read. The app
+  applies settings, chooses a valid explicit hash route or otherwise restores
+  the last stable context, then renders that view.
+- [ ] Startup never reopens transient About, Help, or Settings overlays.
+- [ ] An unknown game route falls back to application Home; a missing attempt
+  for a known game falls back to that game's home. Both show a friendly
+  notification and preserve stored data.
+- [ ] Route changes wait for pending durable writes before changing the view.
+- [ ] If IndexedDB cannot open or a required migration fails, gameplay and
+  settings writes are blocked, a friendly message is shown, and static
+  Help/About content remains available.
+
+### Persistence and ownership
+
+- [ ] A user action and its automatic consequences update the attempt snapshot
+  and undo history atomically. Undo atomically restores the prior snapshot and
+  removes that action from history.
+- [ ] Winning or forfeiting atomically records the outcome and removes move
+  history.
+- [ ] A storage write gets at most three automatic retries, each one second
+  apart and in a fresh transaction. After final failure, moves stop and the
+  user can Retry or Revert to the last saved snapshot.
+- [ ] A revision conflict is not retried automatically; moves stop and the
+  user can explicitly load the latest saved state.
+- [ ] At most one window can write. Other windows are read-only; ownership
+  takeover reloads the latest snapshot and undo history before writes resume.
+- [ ] On `versionchange`, an open window stops storage activity, closes its
+  database connection, and presents the approved reload notice.
+
+### Settings and UI services
+
+- [ ] An unset setting reads as its declared default without writing it;
+  invalid or unknown settings are rejected.
+- [ ] Changing game options immediately persists the last-selected values.
+  Other open read-only windows re-read and apply changes from IndexedDB.
+- [ ] Notification cards follow configured defaults (upper-right below the
+  application menu, Fade In/Out, 3 seconds, announcements off, maximum 3).
+  Hover/focus pauses dismissal; required-action cards do not auto-dismiss.
+- [ ] When a fourth notification arrives, the oldest non-error card is removed;
+  if all visible cards are errors, the new card waits. With announcements off,
+  no notification is announced.
+- [ ] Updating a notification handle updates the existing card rather than
+  adding another card; applicable timers restart.
+- [ ] Only one modal opens at a time; a concurrent open is rejected. Escape,
+  outside click, and Cancel/close resolve as dismissed. Focus returns to the
+  opener only if it remains in the document.
+- [ ] The application menu is present on Home, game home, and gameplay.
+  Outside click closes it without stealing focus; Escape closes it and returns
+  focus to the trigger.
+
+### Offline and update behavior
+
+- [ ] Offline-ready is reported only when every required same-origin asset in
+  the current release manifest is cached. The check runs on app startup and
+  when Install App (Help) opens; that page keeps a persistent readiness status.
+- [ ] Background cache repair runs only at the agreed triggers and does not
+  notify unless the missing resource affects the feature currently in use.
+- [ ] An update does not prompt or reload the running app. The new worker waits
+  for old clients to close and is used on a later launch.
+
+## Implementation prerequisites for this branch
+
+Complete these before the first ES module ships:
+
+- [ ] Update the release tooling and service worker to apply the release
+  `?v=` stamp consistently to module import paths and cached module assets.
+- [ ] Update the local VS Code dev-server task to serve the repository root
+  (or an equivalent layout) so the browser test page in `tests/` can import
+  application modules from `docs/`. Keep the test page outside deployed
+  `docs/`.
+
+## Folder structure (provisional)
+
+This structure is a suggestion until the Klondike implementation confirms it.
+
+```
+docs/
+  main.js            app startup and page routing
+  core/              storage, ownership lock, settings, notifications,
+                     menu, modals, install help, update handling, themes
+  cards/             card and deck models, shuffle, deal fingerprint,
+                     piles, move history and Undo
+  shared-ui/         game home page, history list, in-game menu shell,
+                     card display
+  games/
+    registry.js      the list of games shown in the gallery
+    klondike/
+      index.js       the game's definition, following the game contract
+      options.js     options, each marked layout-changing or rule-only
+      deal.js        builds the starting board from the card order
+      rules.js       pure functions: legal moves, automatic follow-ups, win check
+      store.js       the game's own IndexedDB store and its upgrades
+      view.js, klondike.css
+tests/
+  test.html          browser test runner page
+```
+
+## PWA/offline/update boundary (approved)
+
+### Approved update policy
+
+- Download updates quietly when the browser checks the service worker while
+  online. Static hosting requires no backend; timing is controlled by browser
+  service-worker checks, so an update is not guaranteed to download immediately.
+- Leave the running application version unchanged. Do not show an
+  update-available notification, prompt for approval, or force a reload.
+- Let the new worker wait until all clients controlled by the old worker close.
+  It then activates naturally; the next launch uses the new version.
+- Persist gameplay after every action. Apply database/game-state migrations
+  during startup before restoring the saved context. A migration failure must
+  preserve existing records and be reported through the friendly error layer.
+- Do not add backup, rollback, or specialized migration-recovery workflows
+  unless a demonstrated need arises.
+
+### Service responsibilities (approved)
+
+- `core/pwa/` registers the service worker, observes installation/update state,
+  prepares and verifies the required asset cache, and reports status to the
+  application.
+- `service-worker.js` caches only same-origin, release-versioned application
+  assets. It does not own IndexedDB game state or UI.
+- Offline-ready means every required same-origin URL in the current release
+  manifest has a matching cached response. Recheck on app startup and when
+  Install App (Help) opens; a stored readiness flag is not authoritative because
+  the browser may evict cached resources.
+- Cache preparation and repair run quietly in the background when online.
+  Maintain Preparing, Ready, or Not Ready in the persistent Install App (Help)
+  status. A successful registration alone does not mean offline readiness;
+  missing manifest entries mean Not Ready.
+- Attempt preparation on first load. If incomplete, attempt repair again when
+  connectivity returns or when Install App (Help) opens, at most once per
+  trigger. Do not poll or run rapid automatic retry loops.
+- Do not notify about a background cache failure when it does not affect the
+  current user flow. If a missing resource blocks or degrades the feature
+  currently being used, show a friendly notification/error with retry guidance.
+- A waiting worker does not activate while old-version clients are open. Do
+  not call `skipWaiting()` to bypass this lifecycle.
+- Installation-help content is a separate feature from cache readiness. It
+  uses capability-first guidance and retains manual browser/platform selection
+  when detection signals are uncertain. Do not use device fingerprinting.
+- All modules and their versioned URLs must be included in the cache asset
+  manifest. Update/version stamping must remain consistent with release tooling.
+
+Exact release-manifest generation and cached-response verification mechanics
+are implementation details; the readiness criterion and recheck behavior are
+defined above.
+The current starter service worker immediately calls `skipWaiting()` and
+`clients.claim()`; its immediate-activation behavior must be replaced with the
+approved deferred lifecycle.
+
+## Import rules
+
+- Shared code (`core/`, `cards/`, `shared-ui/`) never imports from `games/`.
+- A game may import shared code but never another game.
+
+## Storage boundary
+
+The responsibility split, database topology, and upgrade coordination below
+are approved. Exact durable record fields and indexes are reserved for a
+separate discussion.
+
+### Confirmed constraints
+
+- IndexedDB is the durable store.
+- One shared settings store holds application-wide settings and each game's
+  type-wide settings. Each game owns a separate object store for its data,
+  including per-deal options.
+- A move, its automatic consequences, the updated attempt snapshot, and its
+  undo-history entry save atomically. Undo updates the snapshot and history
+  atomically. Win/forfeit records the outcome and removes move history
+  atomically.
+- Failed saves get three automatic retries one second apart; after that, block
+  moves and offer Retry or Revert to last save.
+- Database migrations must preserve existing records on failure.
+- One application window writes at a time; writes also check revisions to
+  reject stale state.
+
+### Approved responsibility split
+
+- `core/storage/` owns opening/closing the IndexedDB connection, database
+  upgrades, transaction lifecycle, request/error normalization, and storage
+  availability handling. It does not know Solitaire rules or game record
+  fields.
+- A shared settings repository owns reads/writes to the settings store.
+- Each game supplies a declarative store definition (store name, indexes, and
+  versioned upgrade steps) and owns its repositories/domain-specific
+  transactions. This keeps schemas game-specific without letting one game
+  import another.
+- The application composition layer passes all registered game store
+  definitions to the shared storage initializer. Shared storage must not import
+  the game registry, preserving the import direction.
+- Application context/navigation persistence is a shared concern. Its record
+  shape and whether it has a separate object store remain open.
+
+Shared storage exposes a small transaction/request adapter. The settings
+repository and each game's repository build domain operations on it. The
+adapter makes the transaction's object stores and read/write mode explicit,
+and provides scoped requests without exposing connection lifecycle management
+to callers.
+
+### Transaction boundary
+
+Every domain operation that must be atomic is one IndexedDB read-write
+transaction covering all affected stores. For example, recording a win updates
+the attempt and removes its move history in one transaction. A transaction
+must not await network work, timers, or unrelated asynchronous work; IndexedDB
+may deactivate an idle transaction.
+
+The adapter must make transaction scope explicit, prevent writes without
+application ownership, verify expected revisions transactionally, and surface
+failures to the friendly UI error layer while retaining full console details.
+
+Revision mismatches are conflicts, not retryable storage failures. Stop further
+moves, report that progress changed elsewhere, and offer to load the latest
+durable snapshot; this discards the unsaved action. Do not replay or blindly
+retry the stale operation.
+
+### Save coordinator (approved responsibility)
+
+The shared save coordinator owns the approved three retries, spaced one second
+apart. Each retry starts a fresh IndexedDB transaction for the same pending
+atomic operation; it never attempts to reuse an aborted transaction. It does
+not retry revision conflicts. Game repositories define the operation and
+provide the game-specific action for reverting to the last durable snapshot.
+The coordinator reports final storage failure to the UI error layer and keeps
+the pending operation available for manual Retry or Revert.
+
+### Database topology (approved)
+
+Use one application IndexedDB database containing one shared settings store and
+one object store per game. The shared storage initializer receives each
+registered game's store definition from the application composition layer.
+Database version upgrades create or update stores and indexes; game-specific
+migration steps remain owned by that game's definition.
+
+Record fields, indexes, database naming/version constants, and exact API
+signatures are intentionally deferred to the storage-schema discussion.
+
+### Writable-window ownership (approved direction)
+
+- Use the Web Locks API where available, with an IndexedDB lease and
+  transactional revision checks as the tested fallback.
+- BroadcastChannel may notify windows of ownership/state changes; it is not a
+  lock.
+- If fallback ownership is ambiguous, fail closed: do not allow writes until
+  ownership can be established.
+- Explicit takeover must make the previous owner read-only and reload the
+  latest durable state before the new owner resumes writes.
+
+### Coordinating database upgrades (approved)
+
+- Every application window closes its database connection on `versionchange`
+  and stops storage activity.
+- A window requesting an upgrade waits for older connections to close, then
+  performs the versioned upgrade.
+- A window displaced by an upgrade shows a friendly notice such as
+  ΓÇ£UpdatingΓÇöplease reload.ΓÇ¥ It does not continue using the closed connection.
+
+## Settings interface
+
+The settings repository owns only the application-wide and game-type settings
+(layers 1 and 2). Layer-3 options belong to a specific deal and are read/written
+through that game's repository.
+
+Approved caller-facing operations:
+
+- Read an application setting by its declared key.
+- Update an application setting by key and value.
+- Read a game's type-wide setting by game id and declared key.
+- Update a game's type-wide setting by game id, key, and value.
+
+Setting definitions live with the feature or game that owns them and provide
+the key, default value, and validation. Reads return the declared default when
+no value has been saved, without writing that default as a side effect.
+Updates reject unknown keys and invalid values rather than silently storing or
+substituting them. The repository persists valid values in the shared settings
+store and routes failures through the shared save/error behavior. Every change
+to a game's selected options on its home page updates that game's type-wide
+last-selected settings immediately, even if no deal is started.
+
+This leaves the persistent record shape private to the repository and avoids
+duplicating defaults or validation in UI components. Exact API naming, whether
+settings definitions are registered centrally, and exact API naming remain
+open.
+
+When another window changes a setting, open read-only windows receive a
+change notification and re-read the value from IndexedDB before applying it
+live. The notification is only a signal; the database remains authoritative.
+Read-only windows do not write settings themselves.
+
+## Notification service interface
+
+The notification service owns notification lifecycle and policy; a separate
+view renders cards. Callers provide meaning and behavior, not presentation.
+
+Approved caller contract:
+
+- `show({ type, message, requiresAction?, actions? })` creates a notification
+  and returns a handle.
+- `type` is `error`, `warning`, `information`, or `success`. The view supplies
+  the corresponding color and icon/label.
+- `message` is short, friendly text. Full technical error details are logged
+  by the caller to the console, not displayed in the card.
+- `requiresAction` prevents automatic dismissal. An `actions` list supplies
+  accessible, labeled buttons for operations such as Retry and Revert; actions
+  are optional when the card only explains a blocked condition.
+- The returned handle allows a caller to update the notification in place,
+  dismiss it, or resolve it after its condition is handled. Updating retains
+  card identity and resets the auto-dismiss timer when applicable. The card's
+  close button can also dismiss it.
+- Notifications without `requiresAction` use the configured duration; the
+  service applies hover/focus pause and the maximum-stack/overflow rules.
+- The view reads location, animation, and announcement preferences from the
+  settings interface. Callers cannot override color, position, or animation.
+- When announcements are disabled, the service makes no screen-reader
+  announcements, including for errors.
+
+The exact function/handle names remain open.
+
+### Modal relationship (approved)
+
+Keep modals as a separate service and use `<dialog>` for modal content.
+Notifications are non-blocking, stackable messages; modals interrupt the
+current task and manage focus, Escape, and outside-click dismissal. They may
+share design tokens and a small overlay-ordering convention, but do not share
+one show/dismiss API.
+
+## Modal service interface
+
+The modal service owns the dialog shell and lifecycle; the feature that opens a
+modal owns its content and actions.
+
+Approved caller contract:
+
+- `open({ title, content })` accepts an accessible title and a DOM content
+  element, then opens one modal `<dialog>`.
+- The service associates the title with the dialog for its accessible name.
+- The service moves focus into the dialog, keeps keyboard focus within it,
+  makes Escape and outside clicks close it, and restores focus to the opener
+  when closed if that opener is still connected to the document. If it has
+  been removed, do not restore focus to an arbitrary element.
+- The service returns a promise that resolves with the close reason and any
+  caller-provided return value. Escape, outside-click, and Cancel/close
+  resolve uniformly as dismissed; callers do not distinguish the dismissal
+  mechanism.
+- Only one modal may be open at a time. A concurrent `open` request is rejected
+  explicitly; it does not replace or stack over the current modal.
+- Modal content owns its buttons and form semantics; the service does not
+  prescribe About, Settings, or confirmation-dialog content.
+- The service does not expose options to disable Escape/outside-click closing.
+
+The exact result type remains an implementation detail.
+
+## Application menu interface
+
+The application shell owns one persistent top-left menu trigger. It is
+available on application Home, each game home, and gameplay. This is distinct
+from a game's own in-game menu.
+
+Approved contract:
+
+- Render the application menu from one shared component with the fixed
+  application entries: Install App (Help), Home, Settings, and About.
+- Use a labeled disclosure button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`,
+  followed by ordinary links/buttons in a list. Do not use ARIA `menu` roles,
+  which imply arrow-key menu behavior; standard Tab navigation remains natural.
+- The menu component owns open/closed state. It closes after selection or a
+  click outside. Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger. An outside
+  click closes the panel but leaves focus on the clicked target.
+- The application shell supplies item handlers. The menu does not own route
+  changes, settings content, install help, or About modal content.
+- Selecting an item closes the menu before invoking its handler. Navigation
+  handlers wait for pending durable writes where required.
+- The trigger remains reachable and unobstructed by notifications.
+
+The exact API shape, item visuals, and responsive panel placement remain open.
+
+## Navigation/router interface
+
+The router owns stable application navigation and delegates rendering to the
+application composition layer. It does not render game-specific views or own
+game rules.
+
+Approved route model:
+
+- Application home.
+- A game's home, identified by game id.
+- Gameplay for one attempt, identified by game id and attempt id.
+
+Approved router behavior:
+
+- All stable-view changes pass through the router; menu and gallery handlers
+  request navigation instead of changing the DOM directly.
+- Before changing routes, wait for pending durable writes. Then persist the
+  destination as the last stable application context and render it.
+- On startup, restore the last stable context. Do not restore transient
+  overlays such as About, Install Help, or Settings.
+- Keep transient overlay state out of route/context persistence.
+- Handle browser Back/Forward through the same route-change path and save the
+  resulting stable context.
+- The router receives route renderers/handlers from the application
+  composition layer; it does not import game modules.
+
+### Route encoding (approved)
+
+Use hash-based routes, such as `#/home`, `#/games/klondike`, and
+`#/games/klondike/attempts/<id>`. The app remains a static file site; routes
+must not require a server, backend, or rewrite/fallback configuration.
+Hash changes support browser Back/Forward. The durable saved context remains
+available for startup restoration.
+
+On startup, a valid explicit hash route takes precedence. If no explicit route
+is present, restore the last stable context from IndexedDB.
+
+If an explicit route names an unknown game, route to application Home and show
+a friendly notification. If the game exists but the named attempt does not,
+route to that game's home and show a friendly notification. Do not silently
+open a different game or delete data.
+
+Whether game-home UI state such as history scroll is restored remains open.
+
+## Theme interface
+
+Approved approach: keep theming to CSS custom properties and the
+application-wide settings repository; do not introduce a theme framework.
+
+- Define semantic color, spacing, and other design tokens in CSS.
+- The default theme supplies token values on `:root`. Additional themes
+  override the same tokens under `:root[data-theme="<theme-id>"]`.
+- Components consume tokens rather than defining theme-specific colors.
+- If/when multiple themes are offered, a validated application setting stores
+  the selected theme id. On startup, apply that saved selection before
+  rendering; otherwise use the default theme.
+- Theme selection persists through the existing settings interface. Theme
+  definitions remain CSS data, not JavaScript style objects.
+
+One default theme can ship first; adding a selector and additional themes is
+not required until those themes are designed.
+
+## Application startup/composition
+
+The composition root (`main.js`) wires services together. Keep startup ordered
+only where a dependency requires it; unrelated PWA work must not delay access
+to the application.
+
+Approved sequence:
+
+1. Render the static application shell and establish a friendly fatal-error
+   surface.
+2. Start service-worker registration/cache verification in the background.
+   Report offline readiness separately; do not block the app shell on it.
+3. Open IndexedDB and complete required upgrades/migrations before reading
+   persisted application state.
+4. Load application settings and apply theme/display preferences.
+5. Establish writable-window ownership. A window without ownership can still
+   read and render in read-only mode.
+6. Resolve the startup route: valid explicit hash first, otherwise the last
+   stable saved context.
+7. Load the data needed for that route and render it. Keep transient overlays
+   closed on startup.
+
+The composition root passes service interfaces, game definitions, and route
+renderers explicitly; shared services do not discover/import game modules.
+Optional background work (cache preparation, update checks) reports status
+without holding up a usable view.
+
+If IndexedDB cannot be opened or a required migration fails, show a friendly
+blocking message and disable gameplay and settings writes. Static Help/About
+content may remain available. Do not offer volatile-only gameplay that could
+lose unsaved progress.
+
+## Game contract
+
+Every game exports one definition object containing:
+
+- Its id, name, and version.
+- Its option definitions, each classified as layout-changing or rule-only.
+- `deal(cardOrder, layoutOptions)`, returning the starting state.
+- `applyAction(state, action)`, returning the new state together with its
+  automatic follow-ups as one undo step.
+- `isWon(state)`.
+- Its IndexedDB store schema and upgrades.
+- Its display functions.
+
+The shared game home, history, Retry, Resume, Forfeit, Undo, and saving all work
+through this contract. The game implementation guide documents it in detail.
+
+## Shared versus game-specific code
+
+- Clearly generic parts are shared from the start: cards, deck, shuffle, piles,
+  Undo, saving, and the game home page.
+- Everything else stays inside its game until a second game needs it, then
+  moves to shared code.
+
+## Shared-code catalog
+
+Before writing a helper, check this catalog and reuse an existing export.
+Update it in the same change that adds, renames, or removes a shared export.
+
+| Module | Export | Purpose |
+|---|---|---|
+| *(none yet)* | | |

+<!--
+Generated by project-toolkit
+Source: https://github.com/Ignyos/project-toolkit
+Commit: 0c9e12c7b9fd60e297e690b5a3943edabe8dc868
+Profile: vanilla-js-github-pages-spa
+Generated: 2026-10-12T22:06:35Z
+-->
+# PM Branching Guidance (Optional Module)
+
+> Optional add-on to `workflow.md`. Offer this during PM setup (greenfield or existing) as an
+> opt-in choice -- when the developer declines, none of the rules below apply and branching is left
+> entirely to the developer's own judgment.
+
+## Why this exists
+
+Lifecycle state (`backlog/` -> `current/` -> `release-candidate-dev/` -> `release-candidate/` ->
+`completed/`) lives in files tracked by git. Without a branching convention, PM housekeeping
+commits (creating/editing/moving item files) and feature code commits get tangled together on the
+same working branch, making PM history noisy and merges harder to reason about.
+
+## Core principle
+
+Two kinds of changes are treated differently:
+
+- **PM housekeeping changes** -- creating, editing, or moving item files under `PM/`. These belong
+  on `dev`.
+- **Code changes** -- everything else. These belong on a dedicated working branch, never committed
+  directly to `dev`.
+
+## Branch naming
+
+A working branch for an item is named after its id: `<id>` (for example `feat-014`), optionally
+with a short slug appended: `<id>-<slug>` (for example `feat-014-branch-policy`).
+
+## Rule 1 -- Adding/editing a PM item while already on dev
+
+No special handling needed. Commit the PM item change directly to `dev`.
+
+## Rule 2 -- Adding/editing a PM item while on a working branch
+
+The AI must not switch branches or commit on the developer's behalf without confirmation. Suggested
+sequence, offered as a strong suggestion (not a hard gate):
+
+1. If the working branch has uncommitted changes, suggest committing them first.
+2. Switch to `dev`.
+3. Create/edit the PM item and commit it to `dev`.
+4. Switch back to the working branch the developer was on.
+5. Merge `dev` into the working branch so it picks up the new item.
+
+This sequence is a candidate for a helper script (for example `scripts/pm-sync.ps1`) so the
+developer can run one command instead of the AI performing multiple git operations by hand.
+
+## Rule 3 -- Starting code work on an existing item while on dev
+
+Before any code edit, the AI must strongly suggest creating (or switching to, if it already
+exists) a working branch named after the item id, and switch to it before making changes. Do not
+begin editing source files on `dev`.
+
+## Rule 4 -- Starting code work on a task that has no PM item yet
+
+Before any code edit or branch creation, the AI must strongly suggest creating a trackable item
+first (in `backlog/` or `current/` per the normal lifecycle), so the resulting working branch and
+its commits can be tied to an id. Only after the item exists should Rule 3 apply.
+
+## Rule 5 -- Merging a completed item's working branch back to dev
+
+Trigger: the item's code has been confirmed per `workflow.md`'s completion-confirmation gate.
+Suggest merging (or opening a PR per Rule 6) the working branch into `dev`, then ask whether to
+delete the branch or keep it around for traceability. Advisory.
+
+## Rule 6 -- Preferring a PR over a local merge
+
+Trigger: the repository uses branch protection or PR-based review on `dev`. Suggest opening a PR
+from the working branch instead of merging locally, and wait for the PR to be completed before
+treating the item as merged. If it's unclear which mode the repo uses, ask rather than assume.
+Advisory.
+
+## Rule 7 -- Working branch has fallen behind dev
+
+Trigger: `dev` has advanced with other merged items since the working branch was created. Before
+continuing work, or before the Rule 5 merge, suggest merging (or rebasing) `dev` into the working
+branch first so the eventual merge is small and current. Advisory.
+
+## Rule 8 -- Merge conflict while syncing dev into a working branch
+
+Trigger: a conflict occurs during the Rule 2 dev-sync step or the Rule 7 sync. Stop, surface the
+conflicting files, and ask the developer how to resolve them. Never auto-resolve a conflict
+silently.
+
+## Rule 9 -- Item demoted or descoped while its working branch exists
+
+Trigger: the item is moved back to `backlog/` (for example, rejected at the confirmation gate)
+while a working branch for it still exists. Ask whether to keep the branch paused for later,
+delete it, or fold any salvageable changes elsewhere. Advisory.
+
+## Rule 10 -- Switching away from unfinished work
+
+Trigger: the developer wants to start or switch to a different item while the current working
+branch has uncommitted changes. Suggest committing or stashing those changes first rather than
+switching branches with unsaved work in place. Advisory.
+
+## Rule 11 -- Resuming work on an item that already has a branch
+
+Trigger: Rule 3 applies, but a branch named after the item id already exists locally or on the
+remote (for example, from a prior session). Suggest checking out the existing branch instead of
+creating a new or conflicting one. Advisory.
+
+## Rule 12 -- One branch spanning multiple items
+
+Trigger: a single change legitimately addresses more than one tracked item. Suggest either naming
+the branch after both ids (for example `bug-014-bug-015`) or asking whether the items should be
+split or consolidated into one. Advisory.
+
+## Rule 13 -- Branching off another working branch (dependency chain)
+
+Trigger: an item's work depends on unmerged changes in another item's working branch. Suggest
+branching from that other working branch rather than from `dev`, and flag the dependency so merge
+order is preserved (the dependency must merge before or alongside the dependent item). Advisory.
+
+## Rule 14 -- Temptation to commit a small code fix directly to dev
+
+Trigger: the developer wants to skip a working branch for a change that feels too small to bother
+with one. Still strongly suggest a working branch tied to an item id, so the PM-housekeeping /
+code separation from the Core principle holds regardless of change size. Advisory.
+
+## Rule 15 -- Avoiding accidental commits on a release branch
+
+Trigger: the current branch is a production/release branch (for example `main`) and a code or PM
+edit is about to be made. Stop and warn before proceeding, and suggest switching to `dev` or the
+appropriate working branch. Treat this closer to blocking given the risk of contaminating a
+release branch.
+
+## Rule 16 -- Mixed-purpose dirty working branch
+
+Trigger: a working branch has both code changes and a staged or unstaged PM item edit at the same
+time. Suggest splitting them: route the PM edit through the Rule 2 dev-sync sequence separately
+from the code commit, rather than committing both together.
+
+## Enforcement style
+
+All rules here are advisory ("strongly suggest") -- the AI proposes the sequence and waits for
+developer confirmation before acting; it never performs branch switches, merges, or commits
+unprompted. This is distinct from the hard branch gates enforced by generated publish scripts
+(`publish-dev.ps1`, `publish-live.ps1`, `release.ps1`), which fail closed regardless of
+confirmation.
+
+## Extending this file
+
+Add new workflow examples below as additional numbered rules. Each rule should state: the trigger
+condition, the current branch, the suggested action sequence, and whether it's advisory or
+blocking.

+<!--
+Generated by project-toolkit
+Source: https://github.com/Ignyos/project-toolkit
+Commit: 0c9e12c7b9fd60e297e690b5a3943edabe8dc868

+# chore-001: Bootstrap repository
+
+## Scope
+
+Apply the Ignyos Project Toolkit Full Profile in Greenfield mode with optional

+# chore-002: Human-gated deployment readiness
+
+## Status and scope
+
+**Not complete.** This checklist tracks the external setup and live verification
+excluded from the locally approved bootstrap. No steps below have been performed
+by creating this file.
+
+Gate 3 domain verification and HTTPS enforcement are complete for both custom
+domains. Gates 4-6 remain pending; neither deployment nor this item is complete.
+
+Working branch: `chore-002-deployment-setup`.
+Dependency: approved bootstrap commit `b5d4001` on `chore-001-bootstrap`. This
+branch is based on that unmerged implementation branch. Integrate the bootstrap
+before or alongside this chore; do not assume local `dev` or remote `main`
+already contains it.
+
+Canonical target values come from `../../deploy-config.psd1`.
+Publishing behavior and setup instructions are in `../../README.md`;
+PM lifecycle and branch discipline remain owned by `../workflow.md` and
+`../branching.md`.
+
+## Human-in-the-middle protocol
+
+- Work through the gates in order; a checklist is not permission to execute.
+- At each gate, inspect the present state read-only, summarize the proposed
+  single action and its effect, then ask the owner with the interactive question
+  tool. Wait for that specific answer before any external mutation.
+- Ask one question at a time. Use proceed, defer, or stop choices. Approval of
+  this checklist, or of a previous gate, does not authorize later actions.
+- Never request a token value in chat, logs, or a tracked file. The owner enters
+  secrets through GitHub's secure UI or a secure interactive CLI prompt.
+- When a publish script asks for input, relay the exact decision to the owner
+  interactively. Do not automate `Read-Host`, simulate approval, or feed canned
+  answers for real deployments.
+- Use no more than two bounded verification attempts per gate. Stop on a
+  cancellation, repeated failure, conflict, or unexpected target; record the
+  evidence and ask for direction instead of expanding scope.
+- Check a box only after its stated result is observed. Record timestamp,
+  non-secret evidence (run URL, hostname, branch/SHA), and the owner's decision.
+  A configured setting is not proof of a successful deployment.
+- Keep this item in `current/` until the owner explicitly confirms all acceptance
+  criteria. Split PM housekeeping from code changes per the branching policy;
+  obtain approval before committing, switching, merging, or pushing.
+
+## Gate 1: Repository integration and permissions
+
+Read-only starting evidence: production Pages was configured for `main` / `docs`;
+the external dev repository existed. A later exact Pages inspection found dev
+also using `main` / `docs`, not the required repository root. Reinspect before acting.
+
+- [x] Owner confirms repository access, review/branch-protection policy, and who
+  will perform merges. Do not assume direct merges are permitted.
+- [x] Ask separately for permission to push the bootstrap branch, then to open
+  its PR or perform the chosen integration into `dev`.
+- [x] Verify remote `dev` contains the approved bootstrap and its two workflows.
+  If integration triggers a dev workflow before secrets exist, record that
+  expected blocked run; do not treat it as deployment success.
+- [x] Decide how to route this chore's PM housekeeping through `dev` without
+  mixing it with unrelated code, and integrate the checklist using that policy.
+
+Completion evidence: remote branch/SHA and reviewed integration URL or owner
+confirmation. No deployment is considered successful at this gate.
+
+## Gate 2: Secure development deployment credentials
+
+- [x] Owner confirms the intended external dev repository matches configuration
+  and may have its `main` branch replaced by orphan deployment snapshots.
+- [x] Ask the owner to set source-repository `DEV_PAGES_REPO` to the configured
+  external repository using the GitHub secret UI or secure CLI interaction.
+- [x] Ask the owner to create/select a least-privilege token restricted to the
+  external dev repository's required write permissions, then enter it as source
+  secret `DEV_PAGES_TOKEN`. Do not print, copy, or store the token.
+- [x] Read-only inspection confirms both secret **names** exist, Actions is
+  enabled, and the approved deployment action is allowed. Secret values cannot
+  be read back; successful deployment is the operational token check.
+
+Completion evidence: secret names present and owner attestation of target/token
+scope. No token value belongs in the evidence log.
+
+## Gate 3: Pages, domains, DNS, and HTTPS
+
+Perform each domain/DNS change as its own approved action. Show exact current
+and desired values first; never overwrite unrelated DNS records.
+
+- [x] Reconfirm source production Pages uses `main` / `docs`, never `dev`.
+- [x] Owner approves and configures the production Pages custom domain matching

+  dev site remains a separate preview after the production release.
+

+# PM Workflow Rules
+
+`project-management.md` is a pure index. This file owns the rules. See `AGENTS.md` for current
+direction and priorities -- this file only defines process.
+
+## Lifecycle
+
+`backlog/` -> `current/` -> `release-candidate-dev/` -> `release-candidate/` -> `completed/`
+
+Moving an item between folders is a plain file move. Its id (for example `bug-001`, `feat-002`)
+never changes.
+
+## Ids and prefixes
+
+Per-prefix counters, not a global counter: `bug-001`, `bug-002`, ... and `feat-001`, `feat-002`, ...
+counted separately. Starter prefixes: `bug`, `feat`, `chore`, `task`, `spike`.
+
+## Completion confirmation
+
+Work is done in slices. A slice may cover one item or several. A slice is bounded by the work
+actually performed -- it is never sized to reduce how often the developer is asked.
+
+- An item is never marked complete, and never leaves `current/`, on AI judgment alone.
+- At the end of a slice the AI stops and presents one confirmation request listing every item that
+  slice touched. For each item it states what changed, how it was verified, and what was not
+  covered.
+- The developer answers per item. A single approval covering the whole list is allowed only when
+  the developer gives it explicitly; it is never assumed from silence or from a general "looks good".
+- Confirmed: update the item file, then perform the folder move.
+- Rejected: the item stays where it is and the feedback is appended to its item file so the next
+  session does not relitigate it.
+- Request first, write second. Marking an item complete in the same turn as asking defeats the gate.
+- Only items the slice actually touched appear in the list. Unrelated in-flight items are not
+  bundled in to ride along on the same approval.
+
+## Verification scope discipline
+
+An item's existing acceptance criteria define what "done" means. Verifying that criteria stays
+inside it; verification is not a side door for growing the item.
+
+- Before adding a new check, script, or build step to verify an item, state what it is checking
+  and what result would satisfy it. If that can't be stated up front, it isn't ready to run.
+- A verification path must have a stated completion condition and a bounded number of attempts. If
+  meeting that condition requires new tooling, source changes, or repeated retries, stop -- that is
+  new scope, not verification.
+- A failed verification result is evidence about the item's *existing* acceptance criteria. It is
+  not, by itself, license to invent new acceptance criteria, new tooling, or new build/test steps.
+- Sort every verification finding into one of three named buckets, and only act on the first two:
+  1. **Implementation incorrect** -- fix it.
+  2. **Implementation correct but unverified** -- verify it, within the bounded attempts above.
+  3. **Additional confidence would be nice to have** -- out of scope; surface it as a suggestion,
+     don't build it.
+- A cancelled command, a second failed attempt at the same check, or the developer naming a loop
+  or repetition is a stop signal. Stop, summarize what is confirmed vs. still open, and wait -- do
+  not rerun or re-expand the same verification path without the developer explicitly asking to
+  continue.
+- If a self-added check needs its own rounds of fixes before it can even run cleanly, that check is
+  new scope, not verification. Pause and ask whether it belongs in this item before continuing.
+
+## Checkpoints
+
+- Adding an item to `release-candidate-dev/` creates an expectation that a dev build/deploy is
+  coming next.
+- Every dev deploy reviews **every** item currently in `release-candidate-dev/`. For each, ask
+  directly: "did this get verified? Promote to `release-candidate/`, or demote?"
+- A demoted item's target (`current/` or `backlog/`) is decided in the moment by asking -- there is
+  no fixed rule for which one applies.
+- This checkpoint is a blocking step inside the dev-publish script itself, using the standard
+  script-prompt / actor-input loop.
+
+## Production release
+
+- Everything in `release-candidate/` at release time is, by definition, part of the release -- no
+  diff-matching needed.
+- At the start of a new production release: empty `completed/` (delete what the previous release
+  left there) and commit that deletion, then batch-move everything from `release-candidate/` into
+  `completed/`, then create the release tag and push. `completed/` never accumulates across
+  releases; full history stays recoverable through git log.
+- The release script may use both the raw diff and the `release-candidate/` item files together to
+  ground release-notes generation.
+
+## Dev deploys never touch PM state outside the checkpoint above
+
+No other PM folder transition happens on a dev deploy.
+
+## Optional: branch discipline
+
+`branching.md` is an opt-in companion to this file covering how PM housekeeping changes and code
+changes should be split across `dev` and per-item working branches. It only applies if the project
+opted in during bootstrap and `PM/branching.md` exists.

+<!--

+# Solitaire
+
+Static vanilla JavaScript browser/PWA starter, bootstrapped with the Ignyos
+Project Toolkit Full Profile in Greenfield mode. **Gameplay is not implemented.**
+There is no compilation or package installation step. See [PM](PM/project-management.md)
+for work status and [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for agent direction.
+
+## Local development
+
+Requires PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`) and Git. VS Code's PowerShell extension enables the
+Run & Debug entries. Python 3 is used only by the optional local server task.
+
+```powershell
+.\build.ps1
+python -m http.server 4173 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory .\docs
+```
+
+Open http://127.0.0.1:4173/. HTTPS or localhost is required for offline support.
+The scaffold is deployment-relative and supports Pages subdirectory previews.
+Use the VS Code **Build** and **Serve** tasks or the **Build**, **Publish-dev**,
+and **Publish-live** Run & Debug configurations. Publishing entries commit/push:
+do not run them just to preview the page.
+
+`clean.ps1` is intentionally non-destructive: `docs/` is the application source,
+not disposable output. Release audits and PM records are not build outputs.
+
+## Deployment targets and external prerequisites
+
+[deploy-config.psd1](deploy-config.psd1) is the target source of truth:
+
+| Lane | Source | Pages host | Pages repository |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Production | `main`, `docs/` | solitaire.ignyos.com | Ignyos/solitaire |
+| Dev | `dev`, staging copy of `docs/` | solitaire-dev.ignyos.com | Ignyos/solitaire-dev |
+
+Before deploying, the owner must:
+
+1. Create/configure the external `Ignyos/solitaire-dev` repository with Pages
+   publishing from `main` / repository root. The action replaces that branch
+   with an orphan deployment snapshot; do not store development source there.
+2. Set source-repository Actions secrets `DEV_PAGES_REPO=Ignyos/solitaire-dev` and
+   `DEV_PAGES_TOKEN` (a token restricted to writing the external dev repository).
+   Never store the token in tracked files.
+3. Enable source-repository Pages from `main` / `docs`, not from `dev`.
+4. Configure both custom domains and DNS independently, verify ownership as
+   applicable, and enable HTTPS. The bootstrap does not provision these resources.
+5. Review branch protection, token permissions, and action availability before publishing.
+
+The dev workflow rejects non-dev dispatches and mismatched/same-repository
+targets. It overrides CNAME only in `.pages-dev/`; the tracked `docs/CNAME`
+always remains production-only. Non-production hosted pages show **DEVELOPER
+PREVIEW**; localhost, loopback, file previews, and the exact production hostname do not.
+
+## Dev publishing
+
+Merge confirmed implementation branches into `dev` using the review policy chosen
+by the developer. Start with a clean tree. Run `.\dev-publish.ps1`.
+The script reviews every `release-candidate-dev/` item with explicit promote/demote
+input and evidence, updates the index, stamps assets/cache, validates, commits,
+and pushes only `dev`. No other PM transitions are allowed.
+
+`-WhatIfMode` is read-only and still enforces the dev branch gate.
+`-NoPush` creates a local commit but does not deploy. The dev candidate checkpoint
+is a human verification gate for the upcoming deploy, not proof that the push succeeded.
+Repeated publishes in the same UTC minute are rejected, even for PM-only changes,
+so every real publish gets a fresh cache identity.
+
+## Production release
+
+On clean `main`, run `.\release.ps1`. One UTC `yyyy-MM-dd-HH-mm` stamp identifies
+HTML assets, the service worker cache, release diff filename, and annotated tag.
+The script rejects duplicate timestamps, requires explicit preparation approval,
+retires the previous `completed/` items in a separate commit, then moves all
+production candidates to `completed/`, stamps assets, and saves the diff audit.
+Prepared application and PM changes are staged before generating the audit so
+newly moved item paths are included.
+
+The audit compares the previous reachable timestamp release tag (or the empty
+tree for the first release) against the prepared tree, including version and PM
+changes. Notes and historical audit files are excluded to prevent recursive diffs.
+The emitted AI directive grounds notes in that evidence and the
+[style guide](RELEASE_NOTES_STYLE.md). Update notes in another terminal/editor
+while the script waits, then type the exact release confirmation.
+
+If code or HEAD changes during the notes gate, the script aborts rather than
+tagging unreviewed contents. Approved notes/audit are committed, a bare timestamp
+tag is created, and branch/tag are pushed atomically. The tag workflow validates
+the production ancestry, cache identity, audit, and notes before publishing a
+GitHub Release with the notes body and audit attachment.
+
+On non-main branches, or with `-WhatIfMode`, release is a read-only rehearsal:
+no files, PM moves, commits, tags, prompts, or pushes. `-NoPush` on main still
+creates local commits and a tag. Cancellation after preparation leaves changes
+for review; the previous-completed cleanup commit may already exist. Do not
+blindly rerun against a dirty tree or discard prepared changes.
+
+## Provenance
+
+Generated files retain the toolkit SHA/profile/timestamp in top-of-file
+breadcrumbs. JSONC configurations use line comments. A strict JSON web manifest
+uses an `x-project-toolkit` metadata object instead of invalid comments.
+The hostname-only CNAME format uses [CNAME.origin.md](docs/CNAME.origin.md) as
+its breadcrumb sidecar. These exceptions preserve valid browser/Pages formats.
+
+## License
+
+See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

+# Solitaire release notes style
+
+Preserve the origin breadcrumb at the top of `RELEASE_NOTES.md`. Immediately
+after it, use `# Release yyyy-MM-dd-HH-mm`, matching the bare UTC timestamp tag.
+Do not add a `v` prefix.
+
+## Required sections
+
+- `## Overview`: one or two factual sentences describing this release.
+- `## Installation`: open https://solitaire.ignyos.com/; describe PWA installation
+  only when supported by the release evidence.
+- `## Requirements`: modern browser; HTTPS for service worker/offline functionality.
+- `## Documentation`: link to the repository README and relevant user documentation.
+
+## Optional sections
+
+Use New Features, Improvements, Bug Fixes, Technical Changes, and Breaking Changes
+only when the release evidence supports them. Omit empty sections.
+
+## Evidence and writing rules
+
+- Read the entire `release/rel-<timestamp>.txt` and the released PM items.
+- Replace the previous release body; do not carry unrelated old release notes forward.
+- Describe only shipped changes visible in the diff. A PM plan is not proof of implementation.
+- Never describe the initial scaffold as a playable game.
+- Use concise, user-facing language and present-tense verbs; one change per bullet.
+- Prefer `- **Area**: Adds/Fixes/Improves ...` and explain user impact.
+- Do not claim remote deployment, DNS, or cross-browser support without verification.
